# Regreenity

Regreenity is a PlanetHike project focused on cruise-line passenger experience.

## What Regreenity is
Regreenity is a cruise-line guest-experience interaction layer designed to sit inside the existing cruise-line app. It supports passenger interaction, crew recognition, structured live-event feedback, private service recovery, engagement and privacy-safe ancillary-revenue attribution.

## Product boundaries
- Regreenity is designed as an add-on interaction layer, not a replacement for the cruise line's app or core commerce stack.
- Inventory, pricing, checkout and payment remain with the cruise line.
- The default analytics architecture accepts only a predefined aggregate report from the cruise-line environment; it has no passenger/crew source-event endpoint.
- Crew recognition can use a badge photo or crew-participating selfie inside the cruise-line app. Operator-controlled face matching can resolve duplicate names; images, biometric templates and match scores never reach Regreenity.
- Regreenity cloud receives aggregate KPI reports and non-identifying service-health totals—not randomized or hashed person-level records.
- Aggregate cells below 20 are suppressed or rolled up before transmission.
- Live-event feedback uses three to five prepared questions without free text, and the cruise line controls publication of aggregated ratings.
- Adult passengers can send anonymous prepared vibes after the cruise line privately resolves a photographed, face-match-activated adult receiver. Children and same-cabin/booking-group recipients are excluded; captures and sender identity never reach Regreenity.
- Passenger Top Five badges use dense score positions, remain private by default and can be shared only by the passenger. Event RSVPs expose a count by default; chosen name/image visibility is optional.
- Native proximity and ship-local integrations require host integration.
- Offline-first operation is an architecture design direction; it should not be read as evidence of a production deployment.
- Public performance claims should follow real pilot evidence; demo or pilot assumptions are not production proof.
